contexts.evidence: Sections 3.1–3.3, pp. 6–10: neuron walks carry normalized signed relevance; selected-neuron relevance sums their walks.
Definitions 1–2 and Section 3.5.1 identify walk measures, LRP and concept-relevance quantities.
Definition 1, Eq. (11), and Table 1, pp. 7–13: signed normalization, nonzero-denominator conditioning, and CRP as input/concept/output joint relevance.
Eqs. (15)–(18), p. 10, require positive sums; Theorem 2, p. 12, imposes constant column sums for global normalization equivalence.
Definitions 1–2 and Theorem 2 support the signed-walk comparison and the need to match normalization conventions.
Definition 2, Eq. (9), and Section 3.5.1 supply neuron-set queries; the proposed game extension is explicitly prospective.

notes: Read Sections 3.1–3.5 against every NRM citation context. No textual correction needed. The paper sets conditional relevance to zero for a zero denominator; the thesis correctly limits its ratio statement to nonzero relevance.

verified_metadata.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

artifact.version_note: Official NeurIPS 2019 proceedings PDF. Title page gives Arun Sai Suggala and Pradeep Ravikumar, while the proceedings landing page/BibTeX shortens Suggala and adds K to Ravikumar.

contexts.evidence: Sections 2–3 define infidelity and sensitivity; this source is attached specifically to complexity in the list, although its metric is robustness.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Replace “robustness, and complexity \parencite{Bhatt2020complexity,Yeh2019}” with “robustness \parencite{Yeh2019}, and complexity \parencite{Bhatt2020complexity}”.

contexts.evidence: Definition 3.1, p. 5, defines max-sensitivity and Monte Carlo estimation. The mean analogue, normalization and selected sample settings are evaluator choices.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Replace the opening with: “Using the max-sensitivity of \textcite{Yeh2019} and its mean analogue, the evaluator regenerates attributions on the same $N_s = 50$ inputs for both metrics,” and retain the stated formula and settings.

notes: Original metadata identifies the right authors and paper; suggested author spelling expands Suggala to the final PDF form. NeurIPS official BibTeX leaves pages blank; the existing 10965–10976 range is corroborated by the first author dissertation and retained. No publication DOI verified. AvgS is also implemented and attributed to Yeh/Bhatt by Quantus; the narrow wording proposal prevents crediting the original paper with the exact evaluator formula.
